newsitem.title: LEBANON: Beirut charges seven in German toxic waste deal.
newsitem.headline: Beirut charges seven in German toxic waste deal.

text.p: Lebanese judicial authorities on Wednesday charged seven people, including a German and a Dutch national, with illegally shipping some 680 tonnes of toxic plastic waste from Germany to Beirut.

Magistrate Abdullah Bitar charged Bernd Bretzing, a German, a Dutchman, four Lebanese men and a German-based Jordanian businessman with involvement in "importing 36 containers of plastic waste contaminated with poisonous chemical compounds".
If convicted, they face up to five years in jail with hard labour. Of the seven charged, only two of the Lebanese have been arrested.
The indictment quoted Interpol as saying that Bretzing had been arrested in the past on charges of fraud and embezzlement.
International environmental group Greenpeace said Bretzing was the manager of Hagen-based RC Reifenrecycling which it said was one of two German firms that shipped the waste to Beirut.
Bretzing was arrested in Germany last August on charges of illegal storage of dangerous waste there, Greenpeace Lebanon campaigner Fouad Hamdan said in a statement on Wednesday.
Hamdan said German authorities were procrastinating on the issue of the waste. He said they should take back the 36 containers seized at Beirut port quickly.
He dismissed as untrue what he called German officials' claims that there was no proof the containers contain a mix of plastic and chemical waste.

"There is no technology in Lebanon that can deal with this sort of waste as some of it is contaminated with chemical compounds like pesticides and fertilizers, and some of it is biologically contaminated hospital waste," Hamdan said.
